headline: Computational models link chromatin architecture, nucleosome dynamics and cancer eccDNAs
label: Computational Chromatin And Cancer Genomics
summary: Deep learning and MD-based methods now predict chromatin contacts, nucleosome allostery, and cancer eccDNAs from binding, dynamics, and sequence data.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference of chromatin organization and its cancer-associated correlates from sequence, binding, and simulation data. ChIANet predicts protein-mediated contact maps and loops from binding profiles across functional contexts, while ChIP-FRiP reprocesses 140 cohesin ChIP-seq datasets and models antibody background to correct cohesin positioning at CTCF sites. CONDACT extends this to structure, quantifying time-resolved kinetic correlations from molecular dynamics simulations of nucleosome core particles to map allosteric communication. chromIDEAS groups chromatin states into functionally coherent clusters using epigenetic composition and genomic distribution, applied to THP1 leukemia. DeepECC models breakpoint-flanking sequences to predict cancer eccDNAs genome-wide. What is new is the emphasis on predictive, genome-wide models that either correct technical background or derive mechanistic readouts from simulation.
